title: Telework changes travel and place demand faster than planning systems can adjust
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office GAO-26-107532; telework, travel patterns, transit, real estate, MPO response, and DOT planning guidance
geography: United States communities within 410 metropolitan planning organization boundaries; 2019–2024 data and planning actions through March 2025

observations.period: 2019–2024; telework and travel context across communities over 50,000 people

denominator.unit: metropolitan planning organizations surveyed; 86% response rate

telework_level.value: average telework rates remained about twice 2019 levels across large, medium, and small communities

geographic_concentration.value: average increases were highest in communities with populations of 1 million or more

system_surfaces.value: changes were reported in transit ridership and fare revenue, when and where people drove, and commercial-real-estate and housing demand away from some central business districts

observations.method: GAO analysis of telework and transportation data from 2019–2024, survey of 410 MPOs, literature and federal-document review, and interviews with nine selected MPOs.
observations.uncertainty: Average community telework rates do not identify worker-level exposure, occupation, employer policy, care, income, housing, or non-teleworker burden; simultaneous pandemic, migration, service, fuel, and employer changes prevent a universal causal claim.
observations.subgroup: Communities within MPO boundaries, with size comparisons and selected MPO responses; telework access varies across workers and occupations.
observations.counterinterpretation: Telework can reduce one commute while shifting travel to other times or purposes; transit and real-estate changes can reflect multiple shocks and may benefit some households or places while burdening others.

observations.period: 2019–2024; transit and community response across 352 responding MPOs

denominator.unit: MPOs responding to the relevant survey items; not every MPO answered every question

large_transit_city_recovery.unit: of 26 largest transit cities with 2024 ridership above 2019 levels

service_response.value: more than half of MPOs reported transit providers improved or increased service to attract riders

planning_uncertainty.value: about one-third of MPOs reported they did not intend, or did not know how, to incorporate telework into planning

guidance_demand.unit: percent of MPOs wanting more DOT guidance on incorporating telework into forecasting

observations.method: GAO survey of MPO actions and planning practices, selected transit-city ridership comparison, and review of studies and agency materials.
observations.uncertainty: Reported actions are not common treatments and do not establish improved ridership, revenue, reliability, access, congestion, emissions, land use, or household welfare; selected 26-city ridership is not all transit modes or communities.
observations.subgroup: MPOs, transit providers, and selected large transit cities; item response varies across the 352 respondents.
observations.counterinterpretation: Increasing service may preserve future capacity or improve access for some riders even when aggregate ridership remains below 2019; planning uncertainty may reflect prudent model revision rather than failure.

observations.period: November 2023–April 2026; federal travel-demand study and guidance implementation

denominator.unit: DOT travel-demand data and modeling study/guidance requirement reviewed by GAO

execution_status.value: DOT had begun related work but did not have a detailed plan or timeline for completion at GAO review; recommendation remained open

recommendation.value: establish and implement a detailed plan with clear steps and timelines to complete the study and guidance

observations.method: GAO review of federal law, DOT documents, agency actions, and recommendation status.
observations.uncertainty: An open federal planning recommendation does not establish local investment error, service failure, or household burden; later DOT execution may change the information available to MPOs.
observations.subgroup: DOT/FHWA, MPOs, transit providers, local governments, and communities making transportation-investment decisions.
observations.counterinterpretation: A complex and continuously changing travel system may require iterative modeling; contracting for best practices can produce useful guidance before a final study is complete.

related_sources.claim: Official GAO review supplies telework, transit, vehicle, real-estate, MPO-response, and DOT-planning evidence with survey scope and limitations.

boundary: This record establishes a work-geography, travel-demand, transit, real-estate, and planning stage. It does not establish telework causality for ridership, fares, vehicle travel, emissions, housing or office prices, vacancy, tax bases, household welfare, political action, or local investment effects.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official GAO HTML report page retrieved and hashed; report PDF, MPO survey file, transit operations archive, and real-estate microdata not retained
